analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. It adds a paragraph at docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md lines 545-547 and a sentence at docs/architecture/security/encryption.md lines 121-122. The prefix-cache text says native recurrent layouts store later checkpoints as deltas of the restored file, and a restore reads that chain forward together. The encryption.md text says a delta checkpoint names its parent only through a keyed commitment, so files of one conversation stay unlinkable without the cache key. It also replaces the 'unchanged' claim about observable DBK3 metadata with 'list it'.

I found no code change and no new attack surface in the supplied evidence. The statements are consistent with T-041 leak #2 mitigation (a): on-disk names and metadata carry only keyed HMAC tags, with nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag. The docs do not weaken the 30-minute TTL, tenant/cacheSalt scoping, KEK-wipe purge, or authentication.

Open questions for later review: the delta-chain feature itself is not in this batch. Reviewers of the implementing code in SSDHybridCheckpointStore and ssd-kv-cache.md should confirm (1) the parent commitment is an HMAC under K_lookup with the salt folded in, not a plain hash of a path or token IDs; (2) chain reads authenticate every link and bind the tenant, epoch and layout, so a replaced or foreign parent fails closed; (3) TTL, eviction and deletion of a parent do not leave a child restorable without the parent, and the cold fallback holds; (4) delta files expose no new observable metadata, such as chain length or file-size patterns, that could confirm a prefix. The T-041 accepted-risk text may need a note if delta chains add observable metadata. That is a documentation-currency question, not a finding.
